item.title: Third Straw Poll for UN Secretary-General Race Shows No Consensus
item.description: Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica has regained the lead in the process to become the next United Nations secretary-general after receiving nine “encourage” votes in the Security Council’s third secret straw poll, held on Friday, Sept. 18. So far, however, the race has not produced a definitive front-runner as UN member states speculate about possible last-minute entrants that the Council can coalesce behind.

item.title: The Connection Between Urbanization and Poverty: How Cities Can Reduce Poverty – Or Deepen It
item.description: Urbanization can help concentrate jobs, services, and investments; however, it can also concentrate unaffordable housing, insecure employment, and unequal exposure to contamination and environmental threats. A recent report from the UN Special Rapporteur on extreme poverty and human rights, argues that the difference is not urbanization itself, but how cities are planned, governed, and financed. […]

item.title: Haiti: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
item.description: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed.

item.title: Nepal floods: ‘Apocalyptic’ destruction signals wider climate threat across Himalayas
item.description: The catastrophic flooding that swept away entire villages in northern Nepal could occur again in the country or elsewhere in the Himalayas due to climate change.

item.title: Yemen’s humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement
item.description: People displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen have described fleeing for their lives amid shelling and gunfire, aid agencies reported on Friday, while highlighting the dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in the country and in Djibouti, where thousands have sought shelter.

item.title: Less than 4 years from development goals deadline, progress shows what’s possible
item.description: For Benin, making progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has meant finding new ways to finance development.

item.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
item.description: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.

item.title: Sexual violence against civilians and POW’s in Ukraine widespread and ‘abhorrent’
item.description: Over 1,000 cases of sexual violence against civilians and prisoners of war (POWs) in Ukraine have been documented from the start of Russia’s invasion to the end of July this year.

item.title: ‘Violence will only defer a problem’: UN Assembly President on trust, AI and lessons from the Rohingya crisis
item.description: Khalilur Rahman took the gavel as President of the UN General Assembly's 81st session amid what he calls a crisis of confidence in the organization he has served – in one capacity or another – for 35 years.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure
item.description: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap.

item.title: Outpacing Foreign Aid, Migrant Remittances Are a Lifeline Ensuring Families Are Fed and Healthy, Says IFAD
item.description: Migrants now send home more money than foreign aid, and this is pulling rural families out of poverty, according to the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). item.title: The Cost of Excluding Refugees
item.description: Without the resources to educate, train and economically include refugees, displacement will continue to drive onward migration
